verdict.rationale: Lium documents a browser-free agent lifecycle. It covers renting via `lium up --gpu H100 --ttl 1h` or `POST /executors/rent-by-spec`, running workloads with `lium exec` (which returns the remote exit code), and teardown through TTL, end-time or spend-cap auto-delete or the SDK's rent-run-remove flow. The agents page states an agent can 'sign up, fund, rent, connect and remove pods' with no browser. The OpenAPI probe 404s only cover docs.lium.io paths, not the documented lium.io/api/openapi.json, so they do not contradict the API claim. The MCP server only covers docs and prices, but the CLI and API paths are enough for this story. Missing for 10: pod health and status monitoring is only thinly evidenced (spend/runway and nvidia-smi via exec), and there is no independent hands-on corroboration of the end-to-end flow.
